pages.title: Websites
pages.seoTitle: Website Builder, Templates, Stores & Design Services | CloudHost247
pages.description: Build a website on CloudHost247 with the website builder or the AI website builder, start from a template, launch a store, or have our designers do it for you.

hero.heading: Four ways to get a website
hero.lede: Build it yourself in the browser, describe it and let the AI builder draft it, start from a template, or hire a CloudHost247 designer to deliver it. All four land on the same hosting.

items.title: Website Builder
items.body: Pages, sections, media and publishing — with a real preview and a publish step, not a mock-up.

items.title: AI Website Builder
items.body: Write a description of the site you need and get real pages, copy and SEO to edit.

items.title: Website Templates
items.body: Start from a layout that is already structured for publishing instead of a blank page.

items.title: Online Store
items.body: Sell physical, digital and service products from the same platform that hosts the site.

items.title: Website Design Services
items.body: Scoped, quoted and delivered by the CloudHost247 team — brief, design, build, handover.

items.title: Hire an Expert
items.body: Request a specialist for design, development, migration or ongoing maintenance.

items.title: Website Migration
items.body: Move an existing site onto CloudHost247 infrastructure with a verified cutover.

items.title: Digital Marketing
items.body: Campaigns, search visibility and a unified inbox for the enquiries the site produces.

sections.heading: A website is not finished when it launches

items.label: HTTPS from the first visitor
items.body: A certificate is issued for the domain you publish on, and renewed without anyone remembering to.

items.label: Backups you can restore
items.body: Scheduled backup jobs with a visible run history, so a mistake is recoverable.

items.label: Hosting that keeps up
items.body: The site runs on hosting that can be upgraded without rebuilding the site.

items.label: A domain that belongs to you
items.body: Register it with us or bring the one you own, and manage DNS from the same account.

faqs.q: Do I need hosting to use the website builder?
faqs.a: The builder publishes to CloudHost247 hosting. If you already have hosting with us it is already available in your account.

faqs.q: Is the AI builder a real feature?
faqs.a: Yes — it generates draft pages, copy and SEO metadata into the builder, where you edit and publish them. It is not a mock-up or a screenshot.

faqs.q: Can you design the site for me?
faqs.a: Yes. Design services are scoped and quoted before work starts, and delivered through the expert services workflow.

faqs.q: Do you offer a CDN product?
faqs.a: No CDN product is claimed here. Where a deployment integrates a provider's services, they appear in your account as the services you actually have.

pages.title: Help Center
pages.description: CloudHost247 support: search the knowledge base and documentation, run a diagnostic tool, open a ticket with the team, or check what is happening right now.

hero.heading: How to get an answer quickly
hero.lede: Most questions fall into one of four places: the documentation, a diagnostic tool, the knowledge base, or a ticket to the team. This page routes you to the right one.

items.title: Documentation
items.body: Platform references: APIs, deployment, environments, provisioning and operations.

items.title: Diagnostic Tools
items.body: Check DNS, propagation, IPs, headers and more — and see the result rather than a description of it.

items.title: Knowledge Base
items.body: Task-oriented guides for hosting, domains, email, servers and billing.

items.title: Open a Ticket
items.body: Reach the support team from your account, with your services already attached to the request.

sections.heading: Four things that make a ticket solvable in one reply

items.label: The service or domain involved
items.body: A ticket opening with the affected service is already in the right queue. The subject line is what gets it there.

items.label: What you expected and what happened
items.body: Two sentences describing the difference resolves more tickets than any amount of log pasting.

items.label: What changed just before
items.body: A deployment, an update, a DNS change, a new plugin. Most incidents have a preceding change.

items.label: Any error message, verbatim
items.body: The exact text, copied rather than summarised. Paraphrased errors cost a round trip every time.

faqs.a: Support is staffed around the clock for service-affecting issues. Business-hour enquiries are handled in business hours, and the published contact details for your deployment are on the contact page.
Where a support phone number is configured for the deployment it is published on the contact page. If no number is published, none is available.

faqs.q: Can I check whether an issue is mine or the platform's?
faqs.a: Yes — the service status page reports what the platform can verify about itself, and the diagnostic tools check DNS, connectivity and protocol behaviour from the platform's side.

hero.heading: Documentation for the platform as it is
hero.lede: References and guides covering APIs, provisioning, deployment, domain services, payments, billing and operations — written from the implementation, including what is not finished.

sections.heading: Guides in this repository

faqs.q: Is there a public API reference?
faqs.a: Yes — the API documentation covers authentication, catalog, commerce, domains, deployments, infrastructure and billing endpoints.

faqs.q: Does the documentation describe unfinished work?
faqs.a: Yes, deliberately. Documents that describe incomplete or frozen work exist so that nobody builds against a feature believing it is finished.

faqs.q: Can I contribute a fix to the documentation?
faqs.a: Documentation lives with the platform source. Raise it through support and it goes to the team that owns the relevant area.

pages.title: Service Status
pages.description: Live service status for CloudHost247: the checks the platform can verify itself, reported honestly — including what is not monitored.

hero.heading: What the platform can verify, right now
hero.lede: This page runs real checks against this deployment and reports the result. Anything the platform cannot verify is labelled as not monitored rather than shown as operational.

sections.heading: Why there is no historical uptime percentage
sections.body: An uptime figure is only meaningful when it comes from continuous, independent, long-term measurement. Publishing a percentage derived from anything else would be a made-up number with a decimal point, which is worse than publishing none.

faqs.q: Is this page updated in real time?
faqs.a: The checks run when you load the page, so what you see is the state at that moment rather than a cached status.
It means the platform has no health check for that component. It is neither confirmed working nor claimed broken — it is simply not measured.

faqs.q: Where do I report an outage?
faqs.a: Open a ticket, including the service affected and the exact error you see.

pages.title: Offers & Pricing
pages.description: Current CloudHost247 pricing, rendered live from the configured product catalogue — plans, prices and billing cycles exactly as configured.

hero.heading: The catalogue, not a price list someone typed
hero.lede: Every price on this page comes from the live product catalogue, so what you see is what the order form will charge. When a catalogue is empty, this page says so.

sections.heading: No countdown timers, no invented discounts
sections.body: A discount that appears to expire but never does is a dark pattern, and a percentage invented for a landing page is a lie with a font. What is on offer here is the catalogue: the plans that exist, at the prices configured.

faqs.q: Why can the price differ from another site?
faqs.a: Prices shown here come from this deployment's catalogue. Where a different CloudHost247 deployment has a different catalogue, that is a configuration difference rather than a better deal.
Tax treatment depends on your location and the configured billing settings, and is shown on the order form and invoice.
The currencies configured in the billing platform. The currency selector on the order flow shows what is available.

hero.heading: Pricing straight from the catalogue

points: Domain pricing from the registrar catalogue

faqs.a: Renewal pricing is whatever the catalogue holds for that product and cycle. Where a promotional price exists it is stated with its term, and the renewal price is the one on the product page.
Yes, subject to the product. Upgrades and downgrades are handled from your account and prorated according to the billing configuration.

pages.title: Security & Compliance
pages.description: How CloudHost247 secures its platform and customer data: authentication, access control, encryption, isolation, logging and responsible disclosure.

hero.heading: Security stated as practice, not as decoration
hero.lede: What we actually do to protect accounts, data and infrastructure — and what we deliberately do not claim, because a badge is not a control.
points: Encryption in transit and at rest

items.title: Authentication
items.body: Password hashing with a memory-hard algorithm, multi-factor authentication by TOTP, and passkey (WebAuthn) sign-in as a phishing-resistant option.

items.title: Least privilege
items.body: Role-based access for administrative functions, re-verified server-side on every request rather than trusted from the interface.

items.title: Encryption
items.body: TLS for every public endpoint and mail transport, with certificates issued and renewed automatically; sensitive values encrypted at rest.

items.title: Isolation
items.body: Customer services are separated, and provider credentials are held encrypted and used only by platform operations.

items.title: Logging and audit
items.body: Authentication events, administrative actions and infrastructure operations are recorded, giving an answer to who did what and when.

items.title: Response
items.body: A defined incident path: detection, containment, notification and review — documented before it is needed.

items.label: Tell us, privately
items.body: Report through the contact route with enough detail to reproduce it. Do not test against another customer's service or data.

items.label: We will acknowledge and investigate
items.body: Reports are triaged, and you get a response from a person who can act on it rather than an automated reply.

items.label: Do not access data that is not yours
items.body: Proof of concept that stops at the boundary of your own account is welcome. Going further is not authorised, whatever the intention.

sections.heading: Certifications we do not claim
sections.body: Where a compliance framework matters to you — ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA — ask, and you will get an accurate answer including 'not certified'. Publishing a certification we do not hold would be the single most damaging thing this page could do.

faqs.a: Yes — TOTP-based multi-factor authentication and WebAuthn passkeys are both supported on accounts.
Data is isolated per service, encrypted in transit, and access is role-restricted and logged. The Data Protection Standards document describes the controls in more detail.
In the regions configured for the services you use. The data centres page lists the regions this deployment can actually deploy into.

faqs.q: Can you complete a security questionnaire?
faqs.a: Yes. Send it through the contact route and you will get answers to the questions that can be answered, and a clear 'not applicable' or 'not held' where that is the truth.

pages.title: About CloudHost247
pages.seoTitle: About CloudHost247 — Hosting, Cloud, Domains & Platforms
pages.description: CloudHost247 Isc. builds and operates hosting, cloud, domain, application, website and developer platforms for businesses and developers worldwide.

hero.heading: One platform for everything after the idea
hero.lede: CloudHost247 exists to remove the gap between having an idea and running it: register the domain, host the site, deploy the application, run the server, connect the API — in one account, with one support relationship.

items.title: Say what is true
items.body: No invented uptime figures, no certifications we do not hold, no data centre pins on a decorative map. Where something is not available, the product page says so.

items.title: Show, do not imply
items.body: Prices come from the catalogue, locations come from configuration, and a service status page reports only checks the platform can actually run.

items.title: Operate what we sell
items.body: Provisioning, monitoring, DNS, certificates, backups and reconciliation are platform features, not arrangements with somebody else.

items.title: One relationship
items.body: A domain problem, a server problem and a billing problem are the same support conversation rather than three vendors pointing at each other.

items.title: Open about the seams
items.body: Documentation describes what is finished and what is not, so nobody builds on a feature that exists only in a roadmap.

items.title: Protect the boring things
items.body: Strong credentials, encryption everywhere, least-privilege administration and logs that answer questions after the fact.

items.title: Domains
items.body: Search, registration, transfer, DNS and the registrar toolkit.

items.title: Hosting

items.title: Platforms

items.title: Developers
